Fix Windows PATH-resolution crash in Client.resolveExecutable

findInPath split PATH on POSIX ':', which shreds Windows' ';'-separated
PATH (itself full of ':' after every drive letter) into non-absolute
fragments. Io.Dir.accessAbsolute asserts its input is absolute, so this
panicked with "reached unreachable code" on every language-server
startup on Windows — independent of the Io.Group/std.Thread threading
mechanism, which is why the earlier threading revert didn't help.
Windows GUI apps already inherit the full session PATH, so this whole
resolver (built to work around a macOS/Linux-only PATH gap) is
unnecessary there; short-circuit it like the zig plugin's own
equivalent resolver already does.

Reintroduce Io.Group-based LSP client threading

Reverts 9944851e2. That commit swapped Client.zig's Io.Group/pooled-worker
task dispatch for plain std.Thread as a diagnostic step while chasing the
Windows hover crash — the real cause turned out to be unrelated (PATH
splitting on POSIX ':' in resolveExecutable, fixed in 91ebfe3d5): the
crash reproduced identically under both threading models, which rules out

Swap cmark-gfm for md4c

cmark-gfm cannot build for wasm32-freestanding: it needs libc across ~20
translation units, and that target ships no libc at all, not even headers.
md4c is one C file whose whole libc surface is malloc/free/realloc/qsort/
bsearch/str*, which fizzyedit/md4zig supplies a shim for — so the markdown
preview can finally exist in the web build.

md4c is a push parser, so `md/ast.zig` rebuilds the tree the renderer needs
from its event stream: one arena, entities resolved, and the runs md4c splits
at every escape merged back into one text node.

Two things get better on the way. Tables, strikethrough and task lists are
ordinary node types now instead of nodes identified by a type *string*, which
retires `ext_node_kinds`, `task_items` and the string comparisons that fed
them. And nodes carry source byte spans rather than line/column pairs, so
block extents and `wikilink_scan`'s `[[A]]`-vs-`\[\[A]]` test read the source
directly — `LineIndex` moves to `ast.zig` and loses the half only the old
reconstruction used.

Behaviour changes: no smart punctuation (md4c has no CMARK_OPT_SMART; GitHub
does not smart-punctuate either), and footnotes now come from md4c's own
extension. `Flags.github` picks the dialect, so the feature set is one
declaration rather than a scatter of flags.

Build the markdown preview into the web app

With md4c in place the plugin compiles for wasm32-freestanding, so register it
there too and add it to the web build's static plugin set.

Two capabilities the browser does not have are gated rather than worked
around, each behind a named flag so the seam is findable: remote images
(`net_image.fetch_supported`) need an HTTP client and a worker thread, and
local images (`render_ast.local_files_supported`) need `posix.AT`, which
wasm32-freestanding lacks. Both fall back to the placeholder the preview
already draws when a fetch fails. Wiring the browser's `fetch` into a real
`std.Io` turns the first back on, and that is the same seam the plugin store's
catalog fetch is waiting for.

dvui's `id_extra` is `usize`, 32-bit here, so the u64 the SDK passes for ABI
stability is truncated — it is an id salt, so narrowing is the right semantic.

* Phase 1: layout spike — region-based shell behind -Dnew-shell

Ports fizzy's own shell onto new layout primitives (Frame/region/split) so both
shells compile into one binary and can be diffed live. Experimental branch for
fizzy-as-a-library; the legacy shell remains the default.

- src/editor/shell/Frame.zig: surfaces synthesized from the existing sidebar/
  bottom/center registries, so every existing plugin works unchanged and no ABI
  moves. Keyword matching, selection as a view over host.active_* state, and the
  generalized cross-fade in f.draw.
- src/editor/shell/split.zig: fizzy.layout.split — intent (side/resize/collapse)
  over mechanism (paned/ratio/showFirst), one implementation per axis.
- src/editor/shell/ide.zig: fizzy's shell as an ordinary layout() function,
  ~95 lines against ~215 of in-tick layout.
- src/editor/shell/FINDINGS.md: the spike's verdicts, including a segfault-level
  coupling (workbench reads the app's panel split via drawWorkspaces) and a
  latent bug in the legacy shell (bottom panel opens at 50%, not panel_ratio).

Verified: both shells build; zig build test / check-web / test-sdk-version pass;
screenshots compared side by side in isolated HOME/TMPDIR on macOS.

* Phase 2: thread *Editor explicitly; globals become accessors

Replaces src/fizzy.zig's `pub var app` / `pub var editor` with private vars behind
fizzy.app() / fizzy.editor() accessors, and threads an explicit *Editor through
editor-scoped code. Adds Editor.gpa so editor code no longer reaches the App
global for its allocator.

  Editor.zig itself:  413 global refs -> 11
  Shell path:          28 -> 0   (Sidebar, Explorer, Panel, Menu, Infobar)
  Total across src/:  521 -> 296

The residual is enumerated in src/editor/PHASE2.md: ~75 refs are callbacks with
no context pointer (native dialogs, the macOS menu rebuild, singleton dispatch)
which need a userdata slot rather than a parameter, and ~120 are fizzy's own
singleton UI modules (PluginStore, settings trees) which are not library-critical.

Verified: zig build (both shells), test, check-web, test-sdk-version all pass.

* Phase 3: AppInfo — one identity record replacing scattered literals

Adds src/AppInfo.zig, fed by build options (-Dapp-name, -Dapp-display-name,
-Dapp-bundle-id, -Dapp-config-dir, -Dapp-registry-url) defaulting to fizzy's own
values, so an app built on fizzy as a library can set its own identity.

Converted: window title, startup log, SDL app metadata, plugin registry URL,
infobar label, settings-tree branch title, output-log scope, executable name,
and core/paths.configFolder — which had "fizzy" hardcoded and is what actually
blocked a consumer from having its own settings directory. core does not import
AppInfo (it is shared with plugins and stays app-agnostic); the directory name is
a parameter instead.

Fizzy's one-time Fizzy/ -> fizzy/ migration is gated on the app being fizzy.

Verified: -Dapp-name=graphl produces a graphl executable that logs "Graphl
version" and writes to Application Support/graphl/. build, -Dnew-shell, test,
check-web and test-sdk-version all pass.

The unified titlebar is deferred with reasons recorded in src/editor/PHASE2.md:

* Phase 4: real Surface type + keyword binding (single ABI bump)

Adds src/sdk/Surface.zig — one identifier plus free-form keywords describing what
kind of place a surface's content belongs, never where it goes — as the
shape-agnostic successor to SidebarView/BottomView/CenterProvider. Adds

registerSidebarView/registerBottomView/registerCenterProvider survive as compat

Frame now reads the real registry: matching/selected/select/surface/draw/region

* Phase 5: pluggable shells + differently-shaped layouts (acceptance test)

Adds -Dshell={ide,minimal,studio}. All three load the identical workbench/text/
image/markdown plugins with zero plugin source changes:

  ide      fizzy's own shape
  minimal  one main region + status strip; no rail, explorer or panel
  studio   Blender-ish: explorer on the RIGHT, short bottom strip, big canvas

studio is the decisive result: the file tree renders on the right and workbench
has no idea. Its surface carries {"sidebar","explorer"}; studio's right-hand
region declares the same keywords; they intersect. No place-name negotiated, no
plugin recompiled.

These are shipped shapes MEANT TO BE COPIED, on dvui's methodology for widgets:
an app uses one as-is and writes no layout code, or copies the closest one and
edits it. Documented in CLAUDE.md, including the constraint that follows — prefer
a new shape file over a new option, and anything a shape needs that only fizzy
can provide is a missing Frame capability rather than a special case.

Fixes a crash the examples exposed and nothing else could have: Editor.
drawWorkspaces (the host API workbench calls) inferred "a panel paned exists"
from "bottom surfaces are registered" and dereferenced editor.panel.paned, which
minimal never creates. The shell now states the fact via Editor.shell_bottom_split
instead of the plugin inferring it — the inversion the Phase 1 spike recommended.

Also restores two visual regressions from the spike, caught by comparing
screenshots: the sash drag target (handle 1.0/8.0 -> fizzy's 10/60, ~10x thinner)

Verified: all three shells build and run; build, test, check-web,
test-sdk-version pass; the plugin velopack-leak gate is clean.

* Phase 5b: fizzy is consumable as a library by an outside package

Adds examples/{minimal-app,studio-app}: two independent Zig packages that depend
on fizzy, set their own identity, pick a shipped layout shape, and produce their
own executables. Both load the identical workbench/text/image/markdown plugins

No build/lib.zig or bespoke fizzy.app.create was needed — ordinary Zig dependency

* Phase 4b: persist and load per-surface keyword overrides

Adds .plugins.<id>.surface_keywords to settings.zon, mirroring how .extensions
already works: a Reserved field, a compose path, and a deliberately tolerant
parser (a malformed override yields fewer entries, never a startup failure, since
this is a file users are invited to hand-edit). Editor loads them into
surface_keyword_overrides, which Frame.matching already consulted.

This is the escape hatch the keyword-matching design depends on — a plugin's
declared keywords are a default, and a wrong default has to be fixable by the
person looking at it rather than by a plugin release.

Verified end to end: writing

  .surface_keywords = .{ .@"workbench.files" = .{ "bottom" } }

loads as workbench.files -> ["bottom"], moving the file tree out of the sidebar
match set and into the bottom one.

BUT nothing moves on screen yet, and that is worth recording precisely: ide.zig
routes its sidebar through Explorer.draw, which resolves the view via
host.activeSidebarView() — the legacy registry — bypassing keyword matching. Same
for Panel.draw. So the persistence half works and the visible half does not.

That promotes the Explorer/Panel chrome split from "nice cleanup" to the next
thing to do, and it is why the rebinding UI is not in this commit: a settings pane

Extends the existing exhaustiveness test that guards Reserved fields against

* Phase 4c2+4d: panel-override guard, and revealPosition moves to EditorAPI

Two related pieces of the workbench/host boundary.

4d — revealPosition is host state, not a workbench service. Every in-tree consumer
of workbench-api used exactly one method: revealPosition. And its implementation
was already written almost entirely against the host (docFromPath,
doc.owner.revealPosition, setActiveDocIndex, pluginForExtension); the only
workbench-specific part was a pending-reveal queue that was its by accident.

Moved to EditorAPI/Editor with the queue, drained once per frame from tick.
Workbench's svcRevealPosition now forwards to it so plugins compiled against
workbench-api keep working. Result: text, markdown and image reference no
workbench service at all, so they load in a fizzy-based app that ships no
workbench — the portability goal from the plan's D4.

Two regressions caught by diffing the port against the original rather than
trusting it: it passed the raw path to openFilePath instead of the canonical
owned_path that pollPendingReveals matches on, and it returned openFilePath's
bool instead of true — which would reinstate the exact bug the original comment
documents ('opened the file, caret never moved' whenever a load was already in
flight).

4c2 — Editor.warnUndrawableOverrides. Phase 4c converted the sidebar to keyword
matching but not the panel, so a surface overridden into "bottom" leaves the rail
and is never drawn: it vanishes silently, which is the one failure keyword
matching is only tolerable without. Now a startup warning naming the surface and
the fix. The guard removes itself once the panel resolves by keyword.

* Phase 4e: extract the shared tab widget (core.dvui.Tabs), and name the two region forms

Fizzy's bottom panel and the workbench's document tabs had the same code twice —
not similar, the same: identical tabs_drag_index / tabs_removed_index /
tabs_insert_before_index state (matching use counts, 5/5, 7/7, 7/7), the same
dvui.reorder scaffolding, the same floating/removed/insertBefore capture, and the
same press-to-select / drag-to-reorder event loop.

Only three things ever differed: what the tabs represent (documents vs registered
views), how each tab looks (icon + dirty dot + close button vs an uppercase
label), and how selection is decided. core.dvui.Tabs owns the scaffolding; the
caller owns all three. It lives in core because the two sides sit on opposite
sides of the plugin boundary — the panel is fizzy, the workbench is a dylib.

Panel converted as a pure refactor: 123 lines deleted, 31 added.

Also makes the two forms of a region explicit, which was previously only implicit:

  "this region IS x"      -> f.region(.{ .keywords = bottom })
  "this region is TABBED" -> widgets.tabs(f, bottom) then f.region(...)

studio.zig now demonstrates the single form (an app that just wants a terminal
down there); ide.zig keeps the rich form, since fizzy's Panel additionally splits
the bottom into several panes. None of the three is a mode on the others — the
difference is which lines the shape writes.

widgets.tabs has no in-tree caller on purpose: it is the plain tabbed form between
those two, and exists as consumer API so the first shape wanting tabs without
splits need not copy Panel.

Note: drag-to-reorder needs hands-on verification — not something a compile or the
test suite can confirm, and screenshot capture is unavailable this session.

* Phase 4g: splits become keyword-addressable; presets pair a layout with its keywords

Two steps toward a base layer that is purely regions and keywords.

Splits register themselves under the keywords their docked half shows
(layout_split.dock), and anything outside the layout that needs to command or
query a region asks by keyword (Editor.splitFor). Shapes no longer publish widget
pointers: 'editor.explorer.paned = side.paned' and 'editor.shell_bottom_split =
dock.paned' are gone from all three. Those lines were mechanism leaking into app
code, and they only worked because fizzy's own shape happens to have an explorer
and a panel — a differently-shaped app had no way to satisfy them correctly.

* Phase 6a: one shared file set, owned by the framework

Two questions this design kept deferring: how does a plugin share *data* with
another plugin without the two of them knowing about each other, and how do we
stop answering that by growing the vtable? The file tree and the tab strip are
the case that forces it — both must agree about which files exist, which are
open, and which are dirty.

The answer turns out not to need a new mechanism. `core.FileTable` is a plain
struct declared in the framework, one instance owned by the app and published as
`Host.files`; plugin code calls its methods directly. No `{ctx, vtable}` pair,
because both images already know the layout — the same way a plugin uses
`dvui.Window`. Function pointers are for calls that go *into* a plugin, which
this isn't. So the sharing surface grew by one field instead of eight vtable
entries, and `dylib.zig` gained the four entries that keep its shape honest.

It also closes a real defect rather than adding a capability. The listing cache
and the fuzzy path index were module-level `var`s in `files.zig`, and that module
is compiled into fizzy *and* into the workbench dylib — so there were two of
every cache, kept roughly in step by a `disk_generation` counter each copy polled
to decide when to discard its own work. A tab strip wanting the same listings
would have been a third. One table, no counter, and `files.zig` is 535 lines
lighter.

Watcher reconciliation moves with it, from the workbench plugin's
`folderPathsChanged` hook to `Host.notifyFolderPathsChanged`: the host owns both
the watcher and the table, so no plugin should have to subscribe to disk events
just to keep shared state honest. A plugin's hook is now only for what it
*additionally* wants to do.

Taking `std.Io` from the host instead of reading `dvui.io` leaves the table
dvui-free, so the listing cache, the ignore pruning and the ranking are all
tested against a real temp directory (`fizzy-file-table-tests`) rather than only
under a running app. One `Entry` type serves both a listing and a search result,
which is what lets the tree draw either without a second code path.

Also here, from the same pass: plugins declare a file's *kind* and the app maps
kind to glyph (`editor/file_glyphs.zig`), so the tree and the tab bar agree by
construction instead of by both happening to call the same plugin; and the
integration shim catches up with the `fizzy.app()` / `fizzy.editor()` accessors
that replaced the globals, which had left `test-integration` uncompilable.

* Phase 6b: file management belongs to the host, not to the plugin that draws tabs

`workbench-api` was fifteen functions, twelve of which forwarded straight through to the
host: `open` called `Host.openFilePath`, `close` called `Host.closeDocById`, `isOpen`
called `Host.docFromPath`. `Editor` described the service as "the file explorer's
programmatic surface", which is the tell — it had become the place plugins met each other,
and every meeting made the workbench plugin a hard dependency of things with nothing to do
with tabs. A plugin that wanted to create a file could not, unless the plugin that draws tab
strips happened to be installed.

The rule the service now follows: a service holds only what its own plugin is the authority
on. What is left is the two questions only the thing drawing tabs can answer — which split —
plus the branch decorator, which is a request to draw inside a surface workbench owns.

Mutation moves to `core.FileTable`, so the table that knows what is on disk is also what
changes it and a caller cannot forget to invalidate — the bug the five near-identical file
tree helpers each opened with a manual `invalidateAfterDiskChange()`. Keeping an open
document's path in step with a rename stays on `Host`, since only the host can see the
document set.

Two fixes fall out of the move. A directory rename now takes the suffix below the renamed
directory rather than the basename, so `old/a/b.md` lands at `new/a/b.md` instead of being
flattened to `new/b.md`. And descendant tests compare whole path components, so `src/files2`
is no longer treated as living inside `src/files`.

The linear splitter folds into `Frame`, so a shape declares regions instead of wiring widgets.
`linear.zig`'s layout is now six statements with no `dvui.box`, no widget handles, no

version it replaces.

a container that subdivides; inside a container it is a leaf that hosts surfaces; outside any
container it is the original edge-docking form, which `ide.zig` still uses until collapse and
peek exist on the linear path. One verb doing both of the first two is deliberate — a container

concept: you subdivide, or you host content.

to end. That is forced, not stylistic: deferring a leaf's close to the end of the layout scope

than beside it. Only containers, which really do enclose what follows, return something to

check added in the previous change would otherwise have reported.

`split` takes no direction: a boundary inherits the axis of the container it is in, so the
direction is declared once rather than restated at each edge.

The sizing model is dvui's, not ours: a child that does not expand along the axis takes its
minimum and the ones that do share the remainder. That is what makes a fixed icon rail, a
dragged sidebar and a stretching main area one mechanism with different numbers. A resizable
region stores **one extent in points**, so there are no fractions, no boundary table and no
custom maths — and a window resize grows the stretchy half rather than rescaling the sidebar.

`dvui.box` is both less code and more familiar.

web installs: our own origin fetches what the author published, and the card says so

**The fetch.** A plugin publishes one set of binaries wherever its author likes,
and the registry records the URLs. The desktop downloads them directly. A
browser cannot: it may only read a response whose host sends
`access-control-allow-origin`, and GitHub release assets — how every plugin
ships — send none. Solving that at publish time is what produced the mess this
replaces: a second hosting story for one target, a branch to push, a CDN or
Pages to enable, and GitHub baked into what was meant to be author's-choice.

It is a rule about the client, so it is answered in the client. The page tries
the URL as given and, only if that fails, asks `fizzyed.it/dl/` for it —
`web/dl-worker.js`, a Cloudflare Worker on a zone that already exists. A host
that does send CORS is read directly and never touches it. Nothing about
publishing changes: all seven binaries stay release assets.

The proxy will only serve a URL the catalog publishes for the asking build. The
request carries the caller's ABI fingerprint (`/dl/<fingerprint>/<url>`) and the
Worker checks it against that shard — the same file the app reads to decide what
it may install — so it is not a general proxy, and the allowlist needs no
maintenance: registering a plugin is what adds it. Tested against the live
catalog with upstream stubbed: a published URL passes, an unpublished one is
403, an unknown or malformed fingerprint is refused, http is refused.

**The check that should always have been there.** The page hashes the bytes and
compares them to the sha256 the registry published, before `WebAssembly.compile`
— what the desktop downloader has always done and a web install skipped
entirely. It is also what makes the proxy safe to rely on: the page does not
have to trust it. `installFromUrl`/`updateFromUrl` carry the hash to get it
there; a `?plugin=` load beside the app passes none, the one case with nothing
to check against.

**And the card.** Install, Uninstall and Retry were glyphs — a down-to-line
arrow that read as "a file landing somewhere" rather than a plugin arriving, a
trash can for the one control that destroys something. They are words now, like
the rest of the row. A card being installed shows the store's own bubble spinner
and "Installing…", which on the web it never did: that state lives in
`web_in_flight` rather than in the desktop's `jobs`, and the card only asked
`jobs`. It asks `isInstalling`, which knows both.

to be using depended on where you right-clicked.

a point and `menuItemLabel` draws a row in it, so a right-click menu is now written in the

  parameter the callers that did not know about it silently did the wrong thing —

  document ids, one preview per pane, dropped when the document closes (ids are handed out

A hidden tab is not drawn, and dvui frees what an undrawn widget kept —
including the text layout's line heights (`_byte_heights`,
`__line_ascents`), without which the first frame back measures the whole
document. On a 57MB file that was ~1.5s of main thread per switch back.

TextEntryWidget takes a `retain_layout` token and retains those two keys
under it after every layout (re-retained each frame: writing a key can
replace its value, and the retain goes with the old one). The text editor
passes a token per document; the document releases it when it closes.

Measured (sample, 4 switch round-trips to the 57MB file, Debug):
TextEditor.draw 6211 → 1310 samples, Font.textSizeEx 5242 → 99. What is
left is drawing the visible glyphs.

a document that lands out of sight is drawn once, unseen

Retaining a text view's layout only helps once it has been laid out, and
a tab restored in the background never had been — so the first click on
it still measured the whole document on the UI thread.

A document whose load lands in a tab that is not showing is queued with
State.warmIn: the next frame its pane draws, it is drawn once under the
pane's own parent (widget ids follow their parents, so anywhere else
would measure under ids the real draw never uses), clipped to nothing,
then the parent's packing reset — the pass a swap's capture already
makes. One per pane per frame.

Measured (sample, 57MB file restored in a background tab, first switch
to it): TextEditor.draw ~1500 → 467 samples, Font.textSizeEx ~1300 → 33.

panes blur between tabs, not just into a loaded document

Every change of what a pane shows now goes through its swap: a tab
switch blurs from the outgoing document to the incoming one, and a
document landing over its placeholder is just another such change. That
makes State.armSwap (and Transition.armed) redundant, so they are gone.
The first thing a place shows has nothing to swap from and fades in.

Capturing the outgoing view means drawing it once more; a large document
can afford that now that it keeps its layout while hidden. Measured on 8
switches to/from a 57MB text file: TextEditor.draw 865 samples in all.

A snapshot always starts from a copy of the frame under it, whether or not
its region paints a background: a document draws none of its own (the
pane card behind it is), and a snapshot without the copy was transparent
there, so tab swaps showed the window through. The synthetic fallback
looks up to the nearest ancestor that paints one.

text: a retained layout follows its view to another pane

Widget ids follow their parents, so a document moved to another pane (or
split) comes back under a new id, and the layout retained under the old
one was not found: the move measured the whole document again.

RetainLayout carries `last_id`, the id the layout was kept under last
frame (kept on the Document). Just before the layout widget initializes,
TextEntryWidget computes the id it is about to take and, if it changed,
moves the line heights across (public dvui data calls only). The per-line
ascents are not carried — dvui keeps their type private, and they only
record mixed-font lines, which this editor never draws.

a canvas viewport shadows all four of its edges

core.widgets.CanvasWidget draws an edge shadow on every side of its
viewport, after its content and at full alpha (`edge_shadows`, on by
default). A canvas goes on past every edge — it is panned, not scrolled
to an end — so every edge gets the "this continues" hint, where a scroll
area only shadows an edge that hides content (drawScrollEdgeShadows).

The image viewer's hand-drawn top/left shadows go; pixi's follow at its
next SDK repin.

a store page opens once, into its loading tab

The store's page filesystem answered every call inside the call, so a
page's document opened — and landed — before the open had put up its
loading tab. The tab came up afterwards with nothing left to land in it:
two tabs, one spinning forever. `DocumentIo.open` also wrote the job id
into a load the answer had already freed.

`Fs` promises completions from `pump`, never inside the asking call.
core.vfs.Deferred is that promise for a backend that knows its answer on
the spot: it holds the answer until `pump`. `Mem` already did this by
hand and now uses it; the pages' filesystem does too.

every view change blurs, as far as the blur setting says

`core.anim.transition` blurs by default, at the radius dialogs frost with
(`Settings.dialog_blur`, published through core.dialogs.style). With the
blur at 0 there is nothing to blur between, and a swap is a plain fade.

blur: halve to a few texels, Gaussian there, stretch back — half the passes

A frost's cost is its passes, not its pixels: every pass is a render-target
switch, and on SDL's Metal renderer a switch is a new command encoder and fresh
buffers. The dual-Kawase pyramid halved all the way to `radius` texels and
doubled all the way back — ~11 switches and ~75 draws a capture.

`runGauss` does what compositors do: the same 4-tap halvings until the blur
left is 2.5–5 texels, a separable Gaussian there (paired bilinear taps), and
the vertical axis drawn straight into the output so it magnifies as it blurs.
`halvings + 3` switches and ~35 draws. σ = 1.45 × radius, measured off the
pyramid's point spread, so every radius setting keeps its look; `detail` mixes
the last two halvings in, matching the old sharper core. Side by side in the
app the two are indistinguishable at detail 0 and alike at 0.3.

Measured (Debug, sampled): blur passes 186 → 83 samples per capture run on
pixi's bubbles; three 900×300 benchmark panes 1.35 → 0.85 ms CPU a frame.
Transitions (`blurred`) use it too, once per swap, at half size.
